products.name: Blackseed Oil
products.subtitle: Cold-pressed Nigella sativa seed oil
products.tagline: The original. One seed, one press, one number on the label.
products.short: Single-origin Ethiopian Nigella sativa, cold-pressed and standardized to 4.64% thymoquinone. Amber glass, glass dropper, lot number on every bottle.
products.long: Most blackseed oil is sold on folklore. Ours is sold on a number. Every lot is pressed from a single Ethiopian harvest, held below 40 °C, and released only after an independent laboratory confirms thymoquinone at 4.64%. Unrefined and unblended, so the color, aroma, and peppery finish are the seed’s own.
products.ingredients: Nigella sativa (black seed) oil.
specs: Amber glass, glass dropper, tamper band
Cool, dark place. Refrigerate after opening.

variants.label: 125 mL
variants.desc: Dropper bottle | About four months at one dropper daily.

variants.label: 250 mL
variants.desc: Dropper bottle | Eight months, or a household supply.

variants.label: 500 mL
variants.desc: Apothecary bottle | The practitioner size. Ships with a glass pipette.

gallery.alt: Dr. Mushtaq’s Blackseed Oil, amber dropper bottle on marble beside Nigella sativa flowers and seeds
Dr. Mushtaq’s gift presentation: black box with gold interior, oil, balm, vials and botanical card
Dr. Mushtaq’s collection on marble: oil, balm, sample vials, botanical card, brass dishes and mortar

c: Shake gently. The oil is unfiltered and may show natural sediment.
Take one full dropper (about 1 mL) daily, or as directed by your clinician or practitioner.
Hold under the tongue for a moment before swallowing, or stir into warm water with honey.

Thymoquinone is the most studied constituent of Nigella sativa oil and the clearest marker of seed quality and pressing care. 4.64% is the concentration our Ethiopian seed consistently reaches when pressed cold and released fresh. We print it so you can compare.
Does it taste strong?
Yes. Honest blackseed oil is peppery, slightly bitter, and aromatic. A bland oil has usually been refined, diluted, or stored too long.
Which size should I start with?
The 125 mL bottle is about four months at one dropper a day. The 250 and 500 mL sizes are priced lower per millilitre for households and practitioners.

c.safety: For adults. Consult a qualified clinician before use if you are pregnant or nursing, taking medication, managing a medical condition, scheduled for a procedure, or considering use for a child. Discontinue and seek advice if any adverse reaction occurs.

products.long: The softgel exists for one reason: not everyone wants to taste blackseed oil every morning. Each softgel carries 500 mg of the same lot-tested, cold-pressed Ethiopian oil that goes into the dropper bottle, sealed in a halal shell that protects it from light and air until you take it.
products.ingredients: Nigella sativa (black seed) oil. Softgel shell: bovine gelatin (halal), glycerin, purified water.
specs: 500 mg Nigella sativa seed oil per softgel

Store below 25 °C with the lid tight. Do not refrigerate; condensation softens the shell.
Is the shell halal?
Yes. The gelatin is bovine and halal-certified; certification is attached to each lot record.
Two softgels equals how much oil?
Two softgels deliver 1,000 mg of oil, roughly one full dropper of the liquid.

c.safety: For adults. Consult a qualified clinician before use if you are pregnant or nursing, taking medication, managing a medical condition, scheduled for a procedure, or considering use for a child. Discontinue and seek advice if any adverse reaction occurs.

products.name: Golden Hour Saffron Infusion
products.subtitle: Kashmiri saffron in blackseed oil
products.tagline: Whole saffron threads, steeped for forty days in the oil.
products.short: Hand-picked Pampore saffron infused for forty days in our 4.64% blackseed oil. A spoon in warm milk, over rice, or straight.
products.long: Saffron and black seed have shared the same kitchen shelf for a thousand years. We steep whole Kashmiri threads, never powder, in cold-pressed blackseed oil for forty days in the dark, then decant. The result is a deep gold oil with the honeyed, hay-and-leather aroma of real saffron and the peppery base of the seed.
products.ingredients: Nigella sativa (black seed) oil, Crocus sativus (saffron) stigma.
specs: Crocus sativus, Pampore, Kashmir; whole stigmas, Grade I
Amber glass, gold cap, pour reducer

gallery.alt: Dr. Mushtaq’s Golden Hour Saffron Infusion, amber bottle with gold cap beside a brass dish of saffron threads
Dr. Mushtaq’s collection on marble: oil, balm, sample vials, botanical card, brass dishes and mortar

c: Shake. Take one teaspoon daily, straight or stirred into warm milk or tea.
Finish rice, dal, or roasted vegetables with a thread of it.
Store sealed in a cool cupboard; use within four months of opening.
Why infuse instead of blend?
Saffron’s aroma compounds are oil-soluble but fragile. A slow, cold infusion carries them intact; blending powdered saffron does not.
Is the saffron graded?
Yes. We buy ISO 3632 Grade I threads and keep the supplier’s crocin and safranal assay on file with each lot.

c.safety: Food product. Contains no major allergens. Not for use in pregnancy without consulting your clinician. Natural sediment is normal.

products.name: Culinary Finishing Oil
products.subtitle: Cold-pressed blackseed for the table
products.tagline: Peppery, warm, meant to be tasted.
products.short: The same cold-pressed Ethiopian oil in a kitchen bottle with a stainless pour spout. Finish lentils, flatbreads, labneh, roasted vegetables, and eggs.
products.long: Blackseed has been a pantry oil for far longer than it has been a supplement. This is the pressing we are proudest of, in a bottle made to live beside your olive oil. It is not for frying. A thin thread over a finished plate is where it belongs.
products.ingredients: Nigella sativa (black seed) oil.
specs: Peppery, warm, faint oregano and cumin

gallery.alt: Dr. Mushtaq’s Culinary Finishing Oil, amber bottle with gold pour spout beside a dish of oil and seeds
Dr. Mushtaq’s collection on marble: oil, balm, sample vials, botanical card, brass dishes and mortar

c: Drizzle over finished dishes just before serving.
Pairs with lentils, chickpeas, labneh, roasted squash, eggs, and flatbread.
Store sealed in a cool cupboard. Use within three months of opening.
Can I cook with it?
Treat it like a delicate extra-virgin oil: finish with it, do not fry with it. Heat dulls the aroma.
Is it the same oil as the dropper bottle?
Yes. Same seed, same press, same lot testing. The difference is the bottle and the spout.

c.safety: Contains no major allergens. Store away from heat and light. Natural sediment is normal.

products.name: Rose & Blackseed Cleansing Oil
products.subtitle: Oil cleanser and makeup melt
products.tagline: Dissolves the day without stripping it.
products.short: Grapeseed and blackseed oils infused with Isparta damask rose petals, with a touch of plant-derived emulsifier so it rinses clean with water.
products.long: The first step of an oil-first routine. Light grapeseed carries rose-infused blackseed oil across the skin, lifting sunscreen, makeup, and the day’s film; a sugar-derived emulsifier turns it milky on contact with water so nothing is left behind but soft skin and a faint rose.

c: Press two pumps into dry palms and massage over a dry face for one minute.
Add a splash of warm water and keep massaging; the oil turns milky.
Rinse and follow with the face oil or serum.
Will it clog pores?
Grapeseed and blackseed are both light, low-comedogenic oils and the formula rinses off completely. Patch test if you are unsure.
Does it remove mascara?
Yes, including waterproof. Hold a soaked fingertip on closed lashes for a few seconds first.

c.safety: For external use only. Patch test before first use. Avoid contact with eyes and broken or irritated skin. Discontinue if irritation occurs. Keep out of reach of children.

products.short: Kashmiri saffron infused in cold-pressed rosehip, grapeseed and blackseed oils. A fast-absorbing daily face oil with the color of late afternoon.
products.long: Saffron has been the centrepiece of South Asian skincare for centuries; we wanted it in an oil that actually absorbs. Rosehip and grapeseed give a dry, fast finish, blackseed brings its warm base, and whole Pampore threads steep in the blend for forty days. The color is the saffron’s own.

products.tagline: From the part of the vine the winemaker prunes away.
products.short: Rhône grapevine-shoot extract, the plant’s richest source of resveratrol and viniferins, in a light grapeseed and blackseed oil serum for evening use.
products.long: Vine shoots are cut and burned every winter. We buy them from a Rhône estate, extract them, and carry the extract in cold-pressed grapeseed and blackseed oils. The result is a thin, fast evening serum with a green, slightly tannic scent and nothing in it a winemaker would not recognise.

c: In the evening, after cleansing, press four to six drops onto face and neck.
Layer the Saffron Radiance Face Oil on top if skin is dry.
Use nightly.
What is a stilbene?
Stilbenes are the family of plant compounds that includes resveratrol and viniferins. Grapevine shoots contain far more than the grape itself, which is why we use the shoot.
Why evening?
Habit, mostly: the serum pairs well with the heavier face oil at night and leaves the morning routine shorter.

c.safety: For external use only. Patch test before first use. Avoid contact with eyes and broken or irritated skin. Discontinue if irritation occurs. Keep out of reach of children.

This is that oil, made without shortcuts: whole dried amla fruit steeped for three weeks in cold-pressed sesame, then blended with our 4.64% blackseed oil. It is a pre-wash treatment, not a styling product, and it smells of amla and warm seed, not perfume.

How often?
Once or twice a week is the traditional rhythm.

Can I use it as a scrub?

products.name: Saffron & Sesame Body Oil
products.subtitle: Warm-oil massage in the abhyanga tradition
products.tagline: The daily anointing.
products.short: Cold-pressed sesame and blackseed oils infused with Kashmiri saffron and a trace of frankincense. For warm self-massage before the shower.
products.long: Abhyanga, the Ayurvedic practice of warm-oil self-massage, traditionally uses sesame. We keep the sesame and add our 4.64% blackseed oil, a forty-day saffron infusion, and a trace of Dhofar frankincense. Warm the bottle in a bowl of hot water, take ten minutes, then shower.

Keep a dedicated towel for the practice; sesame oil can mark light fabric over time.
Can I use it after the bath soak?
Yes. Applying it to damp skin after the soak is the shortest route to soft skin.

products.long: An attar is a perfume without alcohol: pure aromatic oils carried in a fixed oil and worn on the skin. Ours begins with plantation agarwood from Assam, deep and dry, warmed by our blackseed oil, rounded with labdanum amber and lifted by Dhofar frankincense. It opens dark and settles into skin-warm wood.

Is the oud real?

Why no alcohol?
Attars are the older form of perfume, worn in cultures where alcohol is avoided. Oil also wears closer and longer.
